Mary - Album 1: Bloodlines

Wish You Were Hair

"Wish you were here? No."

Location: Ridgefall City Library
Time: Late night, ending around 10:45 PM
Musical direction: moody indie/skate-punk with dry rhythmic delivery, restless bass, clipped guitar, piano accents and strings creeping underneath; chorus opens wider emotionally before Mary immediately denies what she’s feeling. Final section hard-cuts into horror with shattered glass and distorted low strings.

[Intro — library hum / pencil scratching]

No.

Wrong.

Cross that out.

Hansel said—

…

Why am I writing “Hansel said”?

This is my notebook.

[Verse 1]
Coffee after Linda’s signing
Three cups crowded on one table
Linda laughing, leaning closer
Way too comfortable and able

“Hansel this” and “Hansel that”
Like they’ve done this all before

Which they probably have.

Whatever.

Not my business.

Ignore.

She touched his arm while she was laughing.

…

So?

People have arms.

People touch them.

Normal.

[Pre-Chorus]
Why does that bother me?

It doesn’t.

Smug rich kid
With perfect answers
And that irritating grin

Still hate him.

Mostly.

Probably.

Moving on again.

[Chorus]
Wish you were here?

No.

That would be ridiculous.

Why would I want
That know-it-all
Anywhere near this?

He talks too much
He knows too much
He thinks he’s always right

Wish you were here?

Absolutely not.

…

It is quieter tonight.

[Verse 2]
Then he had the nerve at coffee
To correct my notes on revenants

Not completely.

Just one sentence.

Two.

…

Fine.

Seven.

Then Linda asked about old rites
Hansel answered before me

I knew that one.

Mostly.

He just knew it
More annoyingly.

[Spoken over bass]

Page forty-two.

Correction.

Page fifty-seven.

Add reference.

Page sixty—

…

That bastard.

[Verse 3]
Still I copy every detail
Every source he happened to know

Cross-reference
Check the margins
Add three questions down below

Doesn’t mean I like him better
Doesn’t prove he’s worth my time

Knowledge is knowledge.

Truth is truth.

Even when the source is—

…

Hansel.

Fine.

[Chorus — bigger]
Wish you were here?

No.

Don’t be dramatic.

I have books
I have notes
I am perfectly ecstatic

He talks too much
He knows too much
And somehow makes me check

Every fact
Every page
Every stupid little text

Wish you were here?

Absolutely not.

…

Maybe just to verify one thing.

That’s research.

[Bridge — keys / strings, quieter]

Linda was too close to him.

Stop.

Not relevant.

He smiled at her.

Also irrelevant.

They clearly know each other well.

Extremely irrelevant.

I don’t care.

…

Why am I still thinking about it?

[Beat]

Mary.

Study.

[Verse 4]
Library lights are almost sleeping
Rain beginning on the glass

One more note becomes another
Then another hour has passed

I close the book
Rub my eyes
Check the clock above the door

10:45.

…

Oh.

I overstayed.

Again.

Perfect.

[Outro Build — chairs moving / notebook closes]

Bag.

Keys.

Notes.

Lock the desk.

Lights—

[CRASH — WINDOW EXPLODES]

WHAT THE—

[Music drops into low distorted strings]

Something hit the window.

No.

Something came through the window.

…

Hello?

Nothing.

Too dark.

I can’t—

Wait.

There.

Something moving.

Hair?

That’s…

a lot of hair.

Way too much hair.

[Heartbeat percussion]

No.

Not hair.

Maybe—

fur?

…

[CUT]

TITLE NOTE — STRUCTURAL / FORESHADOWING:
Surface title function: Mary is internally denying that she wants Hansel there, while the final scene pivots the word “hair” into the unexplained hairy/furry figure that crashes through the library window.
“Wish You Were Hair” echoes “Wish You Were Here.” The title does NOT identify the creature or establish any objective supernatural species/mechanic. At cut, Mary only observes what may be hair or fur in darkness.
